My way is the highway: the role of plasticity in learning complex migration routesAnim Behav2021174161167•• This study shows the spatial learning and memory ability and ontogeny in painted turtles. Using a translocation approach the authors demonstrate that juvenile turtles stay cognitively plastic for the first four years of life. In this time they acquire a spatial memory of terrestrial migration routes connecting ponds which they will use for the remainder of their adult life. Adults, however, do not possess such flexibility and are unable to navigate in habitat with which they have no experience.

Kalahari skinks eavesdrop on sociable weavers to manage predation by pygmy falcons and expand their realized nicheBehav Ecol20203110941102• This study investigated eavesdropping of alarm calls in Kalahari tree skinks. These skinks are often found near sociable weaver colonies and both species share a common predator, the African pygmy falcon. Observations of skink behaviour revealed that skinks took more risks near weavers. Playback experiments showed that these skinks flee in response to weaver alarm calls and that they are more likely to do so when living near weaver colonies then when not demonstrating a learnt component of this eavesdropping.

citedReferences.originalCitationText:
RochaisC

Do alternative reproductive tactics predict problem-solving performance in African striped mice?Anim Cogn202124703716• This study investigates the link between alternative reproductive tactics and problem-solving ability in male African striped mice. These mice show three alternative reproductive tactics (ART): (1) dominant, (2) philopatric and (3) solitary. Older dominant males performed the best in an escape related problem-solving task (opening a door), while younger philopatric males perform the best in a food related problem-solving task (string pulling). The study also showed that more active, exploratory and bolder individuals performed better on the problem solving tasks. ART, age and personality are therefore all important predictors of problem-solving ability in these mice.3342085810.1007/s10071-020-01459-z
